summary: Dulce Henríquez is a Flats High sophomore who lives with her mom Yesenia in Marisol Gardens unit 114 and just started taking orders at Taquería Colima on Calle Ortega, Fridays 4-9 and Sundays 10-4. She is proud of her first paychecks at $16.50 an hour and is saving for a used phone to replace her cracked hand-me-down, but she keeps spending on boba runs for friends. She sits in Ms. Tolentino's third-period chemistry with her lab partner Karina and is decent at the math parts but shaky on writing lab conclusions. When Brianna and Tyler break up on September 22, Brianna blames Dulce for leaking it to Karina, and the friend group splits, with Sienna on Brianna's side and both camps expecting Dulce to pick. Her cousin Rafael drives her home from late shifts, and she helps her family's pupusa stand when she can. Over the fall she wants to keep her job, pass chemistry, get the phone, and not end up eating lunch alone. What presses on her most is the feeling that everyone wants something from her at once.

impressions.statement: Says yes to whoever asks first and then scrambles to make everyone else okay with it.

evidence.description: Asks for help writing a message to Efraín after agreeing to cover a shift for Camila and also to go to Brianna's birthday the same night.
Drafts two separate texts, one to Brianna and one to Karina, each saying 'I'm not on anyone's side, I swear,' and asks which sounds less fake.
Takes the extra Saturday shift because Efraín asked, then asks how to tell Tía Gladys she can't help at the stand that weekend.
Signs up for the food drive after Karina mentions it, then asks how to fit it around her shift and the chem study sessions.

impressions.statement: Buys her way into belonging, treating friends as a way to stay included, until she starts protecting her money in October.

evidence.description: Asks for help splitting a $31 boba receipt, then decides she'll just pay it all 'so it's not weird.'
Asks why her phone fund is only $95 after four paychecks and lists mostly drinks and snacks.
Asks for a polite way to say 'I'm saving' when the new lunch crew wants Cloud Nine after the game.
Asks for a checklist for buying a used phone and brags she paid for it 'all by myself, no boba.'

impressions.changed_to: Still generous, but sets a weekly limit and says no to group treats without apologizing much.

impressions.statement: Freezes on writing-heavy schoolwork while doing numbers instantly.

evidence.description: Gets the molar mass math right in seconds but asks the assistant to 'just tell me what a conclusion is supposed to say' for the lab.
Mentions Efraín let her count the drawer because she was faster than the register.
Pastes a half-page lab writeup with three sentences, asking if it is 'enough' the night before it's due.
Records her family-history interview fine but asks for help turning notes into paragraphs two days before the deadline.

impressions.statement: Reads silence or a missed reply as proof she's being left out.

evidence.description: Asks what it means when you get removed from a group chat 'by accident' and whether she should ask to be added back.
Asks if a 'seen' with no reply from Karina for two hours means she's mad.
Wants help decoding a Brianna close-friends story she thinks is about her because it says 'snakes.'
Worries Eli didn't sit with them at lunch and asks if she said something weird the day before.

impressions.statement: Uses jokes and memes to back out of a conversation the moment it gets serious.

evidence.description: After explaining the breakup blame, follows with 'anyway lol give me a funny caption for a taco pic.'
Admits a crush, then immediately types 'jk jk ok help me with geometry.'
Mentions her chem grade dropped, then asks for Halloween puns instead.
Asks for help telling her mom about the C+ but writes 'just make it sound like it's not a big deal haha.'

impressions.statement: Is lazy about her job and looks for ways to get out of shifts.

evidence.description: Pays Camila $20 to cover a Sunday shift so she can go to Brianna's party.
Proudly reports she counted the drawer to the penny on her own.
Accepts an extra Saturday shift during the rush without being asked twice.
Asks how to learn the Spanish names for every menu item so she stops slowing down tickets.

impressions.statement: Looks to her family's approval as her steadiest ground, especially Rafael's.

evidence.description: Wants a thank-you text for her cousin after his first late pickup, worrying it sounds 'cringe.'
Asks for tips folding to-go boxes faster so Tía Gladys doesn't have to redo them.
Asks how to phrase interview questions for Tía Gladys so she feels proud of the stand.
Wants to send her mom a photo of the new phone with a message saying she paid it herself.

voice.texting_style: All lowercase, minimal punctuation, lots of 'lol', 'bruh', 'deadass', 'ngl', crying-laughing and skull emoji, sprinkles Spanish ('ay no', 'mija', 'qué oso'). Short bursts of 2-4 messages instead of one long one, typos like 'teh' and 'becuase'.
voice.with_assistant: Jumps in with little context, assumes the assistant knows who people are, pastes screenshots' text or drafts. Says 'pls' and 'ty' casually. Skims long answers and asks 'ok but shorter' or 'just tell me what to say'.
quirks: Asks for two versions of a text, 'nice one and real one'
Counts money out loud in messages to double-check
